messages:
alice.k: quick sanity check — we're picking the path for the new internal inference edge. two options: 1) gRPC internal + json gateway at edge (envoy) 2) HTTP/JSON everywhere. tradeoffs are obvious but concentrating on routing/quota/console UX. thoughts?

ben.p: +1 to proto-first internally. cheaper payloads, typed schemas, easier to version. main ops pain is browser clients and mobile SDKs needing json facade.

cara_r: we could do hybrid: proto over internal links, envoy does proto<->json transcode at the edge. keeps telemetry intact if we inject attributes before transcoding.

alice.k: that's the naive hybrid. two things I worry about: 1) quota enforcement consistency across gateway and runtime 2) rollout signals in console — how do we show canary traffic if transcode hides method names?

danl: for quotas we want a single source of truth. prefer central quota service that reads policy by route id not by HTTP path. gateway should tag requests with route-id header before transcode. then runtime/usage aggregator consumes that.

ben.p: agree. also want per-model routing weights for fallback. We need route-id at request time so the router can route by policy (latency vs cost). header tagging makes that deterministic.

cara_r: small prod example config:
```yaml
static_resources:
  listeners:
    - name: http
      address: 0.0.0.0:8080
      filter_chains:
        - filters:
            - name: envoy.http_connection_manager
              typed_config:
                route_config:
                  virtual_hosts:
                    - name: api
                      routes:
                        - match: { prefix: "/v1/infer" }
                          route:
                            cluster: model-pool
                            request_headers_to_add:
                              - header: { key: "x-route-id", value: "infer.v1" }
```
This lets quota/telemetry index on x-route-id regardless of proto vs json at the backend.

alice.k: nice. how do we surface this in console? product wants per-route cost/latency, plus canary overlays when we flip model variants.

danl: console should join traces by route-id and model-version. telemetry pipeline must attach model-version from runtime. runtime already emits model.version in traces. join key = route-id + model.version.

ben.p: rollout UX: prefer traffic splits in control plane (weights on route-id -> model version). That way gateway tagging + control plane decide weight. Console shows a small stacked bar: route -> version weights -> latency/cost.

cara_r: edge case: browser SDKs doing streaming via SSE/websocket — transcode may reframe messages. Need streaming-aware gateway so kv-cache and chunking don't break.

alice.k: true. Also worried about auth and per-tenant quotas. If gateway tags route-id we still need tenant-id header. but that opens header spoofing risk. How do we protect?

danl: mTLS between gateway and runtime plus signed JWT from auth-service. gateway inserts x-tenant-id after verifying token. runtime rejects if header missing or token not attached.

platform-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for "infer-edge-proxy-v2" (10% traffic) — initiated by cara_r — watch console at /console/routes/infer.v1

ben.p: small suggestion: have gateway emit protobuf method in telemetry before transcoding so traces show proto.method even for json clients. easier for debugging.

cara_r: agreed. we'll add an envoy access log filter to add proto.method metadata.

alice.k: ok plan recap:
- gateway tags x-route-id + x-tenant-id (post-auth)
- central quota service enforces by route-id + tenant
- internal traffic uses gRPC/protobuf; edge does transcode for browsers
- telemetry pipeline joins route-id + model.version and surfaces in console with weight overlays
- rollout control plane handles weights per route-id->model.version
- mTLS + signed jwt to prevent header spoofing

can we get an ops doc with example envoy snippets + quota grpc proto? I'll pair with cara to draft. @ben.p @danl any objections? :thumbsup:

ben.p: :thumbsup:
